Question: How do I apply for the Blue Line Charity Program?
Answer: To apply for the Blue Line Charity Program, the charity must fill out the application.

Question: Is there a cost involved in this program?
Answer: There is no cost to the charity to participate in the Blue Line Charity Program.

Question: What is the benefit of being a Blue Line Charity Partner?
Answer: The Akron Marathon offers a free, turnkey fundraising opportunity for your organization. Your organization can raise funds without the time and cost it takes to plan a fundraising event.

Question: My organization is not a 501(c)3, can we still participate?
Answer: Organizations must be a 501(c)3 to participate in the Blue Line Charity Program.

Question: When is my application due?
Answer: There is no specific due date; however, the sooner you register, the sooner you can begin fundraising.

Question: Is the Blue Line Charity Program a part of all Akron Marathon Race Series events?
Answer: No. The Blue Line Charity Program is only part of the flagship FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay event held at the end of September annually.

Question: When will I find out if my charity has been accepted?
Answer: Applications will be reviewed by the Akron Marathon. If your organization is accepted into the Blue Line Charity Program, Katie Riley will reach out with next steps for setting up your fundraising page and your organization's payment profile.

Question: Is there a limit to the number of charities accepted into the program?
Answer: No. All local nonprofit organizations are welcome to apply to use the race as a fundraising opportunity.

Question: How will the charities be chosen?
Answer:
Local nonprofit organizations can apply to fundraise in conjunction with the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay. Charities must have 501(c)3 status with the IRS to participate. The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation reserves the right to review and approve all charity applicants and may decline participation at its discretion to ensure alignment with the values and mission of the Akron Marathon.

Inclusion in the Blue Line Charity Program does not reflect an endorsement by the Akron Marathon of any participating charity's mission, beliefs, or values. The program is a platform to support runner-directed fundraising for qualified nonprofit organizations.

Question: How will the Akron Marathon promote their Charity Partners?
Answer: The Akron Marathon will promote Charity Partners on the Akron Marathon website, on Akron Marathon social media channels, through emails to runners, and in printed materials distributed race weekend.

Question: How do I get started?
Answer: Once you have completed the application for your organization, you will be sent instructions on how to set up your organization's fundraising page on Race Roster. View Race Roster resources for help setting up your fundraiser.

Question: What is the best way to recruit runners to fundraise on our behalf?
Answer: A great place to start is with your existing support system. Encourage your board members to run and fundraise on your behalf, and have them encourage their friends and family to do the same. Reach out to your loyal supporters and encourage them to run the race and fundraise for you.

Question: When do all my runners have to be registered by?
Answer: There is no specific date that charity runners must be registered. The sooner your runners register, the sooner they can begin fundraising for you.

Question: Will registration spots be held for Blue Line Charity Program participants?
Answer: No. Registration spots cannot be held.

Question: Will our runners get a discounted race entry as part of the program?
Answer: No. There is no registration discount for Blue Line Charity Program participants. However, the earlier you register, the better the registration rate will be.

Question: What is the best way to promote our partnership?
Answer:
View the Charity Toolkits.

Promote your involvement in the Charity Partner program through social media, your website, email campaigns, word of mouth, and any other appropriate channels.

Question: Are there any special hashtags or handles we should use on Social Media?
Answer: Yes. When promoting on social media, tag Akron Marathon so its followers can see your message as well. Akron Marathon can be found on Facebook, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, and Instagram. Use #runAkron on your posts.

Question: Does the Akron Marathon keep any of the money my organization raises?
Answer: No. All funds raised go directly to the charity through Race Roster.

Question: Does my organization have to use Race Roster?
Answer: Yes. To participate in the Blue Line Charity Program, you must fundraise through Race Roster. When runners register, they are automatically provided a fundraising page and can choose which charity they would like to support.

Question: How will we receive our donations?
Answer: When you become a Blue Line Charity Partner, you will set up your fundraising page on Race Roster and create a payment profile. The payment profile includes your bank information, which Race Roster uses to electronically send the donations you receive.

Question: Do I have to set up a payment profile? Can Race Roster just send me a check instead?
Answer: Yes. You must set up a payment profile. Race Roster needs to know where to send the funds, and due to compliance requirements, the funds must go directly to the charity. Donations are held until the charity provides banking details so Race Roster can release the funds. Race Roster does not issue checks.

Question: Are there fees associated with using Race Roster?
Answer: Yes. Race Roster charges 6.5% + $0.85. These fees cover the administrative costs and credit card fees Race Roster incurs for providing this service.

Question: Some of our donors prefer not to donate online, do their donations by cash or check still count?
Answer: Yes. You can manually log those donations on Race Roster so they are reflected in your total. See the step-by-step guide for entering manual/offline donations.

Question: Is there a minimum that must be raised?
Answer: No. There is no minimum fundraising requirement.

Question: How should my runners fundraise?
Answer:
When runners register, they are automatically provided a fundraising page in Race Roster and can choose which charity they would like to support. Through Race Roster, fundraisers can email potential donors, post to social media, and track the funds they have raised.

Blue Line Charity Partners should rely primarily on their runners for fundraising efforts. The program provides nonprofit organizations with a platform to fundraise without having to plan a separate fundraising event. Organizations are encouraged to create incentives for runners who fundraise on their behalf.

Question: Do my runners have a fundraising requirement?
Answer: No. There is no fundraising requirement for runners. However, runners are incentivized based on the amount of money they raise.

Question: What are the fundraising incentive levels for runners?
Answer:
• $500: Badge on fundraising page
  • $1,000: Badge on fundraising page; free medal engraving
  • $2,500: Badge on fundraising page; free medal engraving; VIP Packet Pick Up
  • $5,000: Badge on fundraising page; free medal engraving; VIP Packet Pick Up; VIP Start Line restroom access; race entry to 2027 race of choice

Question: When do fundraising totals need to be turned in?
Answer: Fundraising through Race Roster will remain open through October 31. All offline donations must also be logged on Race Roster by October 31.
